purpose: Admit, validate, idempotently archive, and acknowledge one delivered Ingest Batch under Wire Protocol Version 1: answer with exactly one Delivery Receipt, retryable failure, or Delivery Block whose bytes match ingest-protocol's own evaluation for a delivering installation, archive the exact envelope and every Source Projection or Source Retraction before any receipt, keep a pending installation's deliveries retryable until the Operator confirms it, and make accepted sequence gaps visible.

inputs.name: delivered_bytes
inputs.description: The exact uncompressed bytes of one delivered message, which the ingress shell routes here when they are an Ingest Batch or are not a valid Outbox Message of another kind.

inputs.name: receipt_time
inputs.description: The timezone-aware Portal time of the delivery, supplied by the caller and recorded as the receipt time and Last Delivery.

inputs.name: operational_state
inputs.description: The Operational Store's installation lifecycle states, honored capability advertisements, archived message identities, delivery cycles, sequence history, and storage reserve, read and written through operational-store@2.

inputs.name: free_space
inputs.description: Free bytes on the store's filesystem, which the store compares with its reserve when archiving.

outputs.name: delivery_response
outputs.description: Exactly one of a Delivery Receipt echoing the installation, sequence, and message SHA-256; a retryable failure with reason storage-reserve-exhausted or temporarily-unavailable; or a Delivery Block naming one closed ingest-protocol failure and the message's SHA-256, with its installation and sequence when the bytes reveal them. The response carries its outcome, exact bytes, named failure, and any accepted sequence gap.

outputs.name: archived_ingest_batch
outputs.description: For a newly accepted batch, the exact envelope, receipt, receipt time, batch identity, and every item archived in one store transaction, with Last Delivery and any sequence gap; nothing for a retry, retryable failure, or Delivery Block.

outputs.name: delivery_block_record
outputs.description: A health-data-free Delivery Block record for every block: installation and sequence when known, message SHA-256, failure, and first and last seen times.

observable_effects.name: operational-store-write
observable_effects.description: Archives a newly accepted Ingest Batch, or records a health-data-free Delivery Block, through operational-store@2; retries and retryable failures write nothing.

owns: the order in which a delivered Ingest Batch is checked, and the mapping of each check to a receipt, retryable failure, or Delivery Block
applying ingest-protocol's identity, sequence, generation, version, limit, and fragment-continuity rules to durable store facts
keeping deliveries from pending, ended, or unknown installations retryable under Wire Protocol Version 1
turning a decoded Ingest Batch into the store's exact archival record
recording Delivery Blocks as health-data-free evidence
does_not_own: wire schemas, exact bytes, fragment-chain calculation, and the closed failure vocabularies, which belong to ingest-protocol
the store's schema, transactions, retry identity, gap evidence, and storage reserve, which belong to operational-store
installation lifecycle transitions and capability generations, which belong to manage-sender-installation
Snapshot Completions, Change Completions, Sync Checkpoints, and capability acknowledgements, which belong to the other accept units
HTTP routing, request limits, decompression, and Authorized Ingress, which belong to the Portal ingress shell
reconciling or interpreting archived records, which belong to later processing scopes
